\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{Exact Minimum Barriers for Periodic Center-Flux Sectors}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We strengthen the periodic $GF(2)$ topology carrier by computing the exact minimum plaquette weight of all 64 center-flux sectors.\end{abstract}
For a sector label $z\in GF(2)^6$, let $|z|$ be its Hamming weight.
\begin{theorem}On the periodic $2^4$ cubical torus, every cocycle in sector $z$ has plaquette weight at least $4|z|$, and the bound is attained. Thus the minimum weights are $0,4,8,12,16,20,24$ with multiplicities
\[(1,6,15,20,15,6,1).\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}For each orientation, the cocycle equations make the mod-two flux through all four parallel coordinate planes equal. A nonzero flux therefore requires at least one plaquette on each of four disjoint planes. Different orientations use disjoint plaquette types, giving $4|z|$. The cut-sheet representatives of Stage 39 contain exactly four plaquettes for every nonzero component and attain the bound.\end{proof}
In the one-representative-per-sector model the nontrivial/trivial ratio is $(1+e^{-4\tau})^6-1$.
\begin{remark}The minimum barrier does not by itself control the entropy of exact center fluctuations or the continuous $SU(2)$ sector partition functions.\end{remark}\end{document}
